opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Alexander (employee ID E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E030.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Alexander (E030) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max access is write (admin only if role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - role: Analyst
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB lists Karen Alexander (E030) as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read unless advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes about Karen Alexander (E030) conflict on employment type: the HR note says full-time Analyst (max write for Source Code), while the Security DB lists her as a contractor with basic security training (max read; write requires advanced training, which she lacks, and contractors can never be admin). Given the conflicting facts and the security record indicating contractor status with basic training, granting write could exceed the allowed maximum. I apply the more conservative valid level and grant read, which is at or below the maximum under either reading of the policy.
